sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Operating Margin Stability: Operating margin standard deviation of 7.8 pp indicates cost swings that make forecasting unreliable.
Share Dilution Check: The share count changed +7.8% a year. Dilution transfers value from existing holders to new issuance.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of 6.6% with ROE of 6.9% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 187 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 3 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 58 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.
